ing: 3 idli (about 150 g), made with batter of 2 parts idli rice to 1 part urad dal, soaked 5 hours, ground and fermented overnight
1 tsp oil (to grease the idli plate)
1/2 cup (60 g) mixed vegetables (drumstick, carrot, pumpkin), chopped
1 tsp oil, 1/4 tsp mustard seeds, 4 curry leaves
Coconut chutney: 3 tbsp (25 g) fresh grated coconut
steps: Grease the idli plate with oil, pour in the fermented batter and steam for 10-12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Open the lid away from your face to avoid steam burns.
For sambar, pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric and 1 cup water for 3 whistles. Let the pressure drop on its own before opening.
Boil the vegetables and tomato in 1 cup water for 8 minutes, add tamarind, sambar powder, salt and the mashed dal, and simmer 5 minutes.
Heat 1 tsp oil, add mustard seeds and curry leaves (they splutter, stand back), add gluten-free hing if using, and pour over the sambar.
For chutney, grind coconut, roasted chana dal, green chilli and salt with 3-4 tbsp water until smooth.
Serve the hot idli with sambar and chutney.

ing: 1/2 cup (90 g) whole green moong, soaked 6 hours or overnight
1 tbsp raw rice (optional, for crispness), soaked with the moong
Ginger chutney: 1 inch ginger, peeled and chopped
steps: Drain the soaked moong and grind with ginger, green chilli, cumin, salt and a little water to a thick, pourable batter.
For chutney, heat 1/2 tsp oil, roast urad dal and red chilli until golden, then add ginger and saute 1 minute.
Cool and grind with tamarind, jaggery, salt and 2-3 tbsp water.
Heat a tawa, pour a ladle of batter and spread it thin in circles. Sprinkle onion on top.
Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil around the edges and cook until crisp, about 2 minutes; flip briefly. Make 2 pesarattu.
Serve hot with ginger chutney.

ing: Peanut chutney: 2 tbsp (20 g) roasted peanuts, skins removed
steps: Mix ragi flour, rice flour, onion, chilli, coriander, cumin and salt with about 3/4 cup water to a thin, runny batter. Rest 10 minutes.
For chutney, grind peanuts, red chilli, tamarind, garlic and salt with 3-4 tbsp water until smooth.
Heat a tawa on medium. Pour the batter from the outside in to fill the pan in a thin lacy layer (do not spread with a ladle).
Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil around the edges and cook until crisp and it lifts off easily, about 3 minutes. Make 2 dosas.
Serve hot with peanut chutney.
Whisk besan, turmeric, ajwain, salt and about 1/3 cup water to a smooth batter with no lumps.
Stir in carrot, onion, tomato, capsicum and green chilli.
For chutney, grind mint, coriander, chilli, lemon juice and salt with 2 tbsp water.
Heat a non-stick tawa on medium, pour half the batter and spread into a round.
Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil, cook 2 minutes until the base is golden, flip and cook 1-2 minutes more. Make the second chilla.
Serve hot with mint chutney.

ing: 1/2 cup (95 g) yellow moong dal, soaked 3 hours
1 pinch chaat masala or roasted cumin powder
steps: Drain the moong dal and grind with ginger, green chilli, cumin, salt and a little water to a smooth, thick batter.
Mix the paneer, onion, coriander, chaat masala and a pinch of salt for the stuffing.
Heat a non-stick tawa on medium, pour half the batter and spread into a round.
Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil and cook 2 minutes until the base turns golden.
Spread half the paneer stuffing over one half, fold the chilla over and press gently. Cook 1 minute more.
Repeat with the remaining batter and serve hot.
Rinse the poha in a strainer under water for 20 seconds, drain and leave 5 minutes to soften. Mix in turmeric, salt and sugar.
Heat oil in a pan and roast the peanuts until crunchy, about 2 minutes; set aside.
In the same pan, add mustard seeds and let them splutter (stand back), then add curry leaves, green chilli and onion. Saute until soft.
Add the poha, mix gently and cook on low with a lid for 2 minutes.
Top with peanuts and coriander, squeeze lemon over and serve.

ing: Sambar: 1 cup sambar made with 2 tbsp toor dal, 1/2 cup vegetables, 1 tsp tamarind pulp, 1 tsp sambar powder (check label: gluten-free) and 1 tsp oil
steps: Dry roast the moong dal for 2 minutes until fragrant. Pressure cook it with the millet, salt and 1 1/2 cups water for 4 whistles. Let pressure drop naturally before opening.
Heat ghee in a small pan, fry cashews until golden, then add pepper, cumin, ginger, curry leaves and gluten-free hing if using.
Pour the tempering over the cooked pongal, mash lightly and mix. Add a little hot water if too thick.
For quick sambar, pressure cook toor dal for 3 whistles; boil vegetables with tamarind, sambar powder and salt for 8 minutes, add mashed dal and simmer 5 minutes.
Temper the sambar with 1 tsp oil and mustard seeds and serve with hot pongal.

ing: 1/2 cup (60 g) mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas), finely chopped
steps: Dry roast the rava in a pan on low heat for 4-5 minutes until fragrant; set aside.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and urad dal and let them splutter (stand back), then add curry leaves, hing, chilli, ginger and onion.
Add the vegetables and saute 3 minutes.
Pour in the water with salt and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and add the rava slowly while stirring to avoid lumps. Cover and cook 2-3 minutes; hot upma can bubble, so keep your hand away.
Garnish with coriander and serve with the orange segments.

ing: 1/4 cup (30 g) mixed vegetables (carrot, peas, beans), finely chopped
steps: Heat oil, add mustard seeds and let them splutter (stand back), then add onion and chilli and saute 2 minutes.
Add tomato and vegetables and cook 3-4 minutes until soft.
Stir in turmeric, garam masala and salt.
Add the oats and water, bring to a boil, then simmer 3-4 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot.
In a jar or bowl, mix the oats, curd, milk, chia seeds and cinnamon.
Stir in half the banana slices and the chopped date.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours).
In the morning, stir well; add a splash of milk if too thick.
Top with the remaining banana and eat cold.

ing: 1/2 cup (60 g) whole wheat atta, plus a little for dusting
steps: Knead the atta with a pinch of salt and about 1/4 cup water into a soft dough. Rest 10 minutes.
Mix paneer, onion, chilli, coriander, cumin powder, ajwain and salt for the filling.
Divide the dough into 2 balls. Roll each into a small circle, place half the filling in the centre, gather the edges and seal.
Dust and roll gently into a 6-inch paratha.
Cook on a hot tawa for 1 minute per side, then brush with 1/2 tsp oil and cook until golden spots appear. Repeat.
Serve hot with curd.

ing: 1/2 cup (60 g) thalipeeth flour, made with equal parts jowar, bajra, besan and whole wheat atta
steps: Mix the flour, onion, chilli, coriander, cumin, turmeric, sesame and salt.
Add water little by little and knead into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Divide into 2. On a wet plastic sheet or banana leaf, pat each ball into a thin round with wet fingers and poke 3-4 holes in the centre.
Transfer to a cold tawa, add a few drops of oil into the holes and around the edges, cover and cook on medium for 3 minutes.
Flip and cook 2 minutes more until crisp. Careful: the tawa gets very hot between rounds, so let it cool slightly or use a second tawa.
Serve hot with curd.

ing: 1/2 cup (60 g) roasted rice flour (idiyappam flour)
1/2 tsp oil (for the dough and plate)
Stew: 1/2 cup (70 g) mixed vegetables (potato, carrot, beans, peas), diced
1/2 cup (120 ml) coconut milk (thin and thick parts)
steps: Add salt and a few drops of oil to the rice flour, pour in the boiling water and mix with a spoon (it is very hot). Knead into a soft dough once cool enough to touch.
Fill the idiyappam press, squeeze onto greased idli plates and steam for 8-10 minutes. Open the lid away from your face.
For stew, heat 1 tsp oil, add whole spices, curry leaves, onion, ginger and chilli and saute 2 minutes.
Add the vegetables, salt and 1/2 cup water (or the thin coconut milk), cover and cook 10 minutes until tender.
Lower the heat, stir in the thick coconut milk and pepper, and warm through without boiling so it does not split.
Serve the idiyappam with the stew.

ing: 1/2 tsp baking soda (or 1/2 tsp plain fruit salt)
Green chutney: 1/2 cup coriander, 1/4 cup mint, 1 green chilli, 1 tsp lemon juice
steps: Whisk besan, water, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, sugar, 1 tsp lemon juice and salt to a smooth batter. Rest 10 minutes.
Boil water in a steamer and grease a small plate or tin with a few drops of oil.
Just before steaming, stir the baking soda and the remaining 1 tsp lemon juice into the batter; it will froth. Pour at once into the plate.
Steam on medium for 12-15 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Open the lid away from your face.
Heat the oil, add mustard and sesame (they splutter, stand back), curry leaves, chilli and 2 tbsp water. Pour over the khaman and cut into squares.
Grind the chutney ingredients with salt and 2 tbsp water, garnish khaman with coriander and serve.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt in a bowl.
Heat oil, add onion and chilli and saute until soft, about 2 minutes.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt and cook until the tomato is mushy.
Lower the heat, pour in the eggs and stir continuously for 2-3 minutes until fully set and no runny egg remains.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander.
Toast the bread on a dry tawa or in a toaster and serve with the bhurji.

ing: 1 tbsp each chopped onion, tomato and capsicum
1 roti made with 1/4 cup (30 g) whole wheat atta
steps: Knead the atta with a little water into a soft dough, roll into a roti and cook on a hot tawa about 1 minute per side until puffed with brown spots.
Beat the eggs with turmeric, pepper and salt, then mix in all the vegetables, chilli and coriander.
Heat oil in a pan on medium and pour in the egg mixture, spreading it evenly.
Cook 2 minutes until the base sets, flip carefully and cook 1 minute more until no liquid egg remains.
Serve with the roti and the fruit.

ing: 2 appam (about 120 g batter), made with batter of raw rice soaked 5 hours, ground with grated coconut and a little cooked rice, fermented overnight with 1 pinch yeast and 1/2 tsp sugar
1 tsp oil (to grease the appam pan)
Egg curry: 2 eggs, hard-boiled and peeled
1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp coriander powder, 1/4 tsp red chilli powder, 1/4 tsp garam masala
steps: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and make 2 shallow slits in each.
Heat 1 tsp oil, add curry leaves, onion and chilli and saute until golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
Add tomato and the powdered spices and cook until soft. Pour in the coconut milk with salt and simmer gently 3-4 minutes; add the eggs and simmer 2 minutes.
Add salt to the fermented appam batter. Heat a greased appam pan, pour a ladle of batter and swirl the pan to coat the sides. Hold the handle; the pan is hot.
Cover and cook on medium for 2 minutes until the edges are crisp and the centre is soft and set. Make 2 appam.
Serve hot with the egg curry.
Pat the tofu dry with a cloth and crumble it with your fingers.
Heat oil, add cumin and let it sizzle, then add onion and chilli and saute 2 minutes.
Add capsicum, tomato, turmeric and salt and cook until soft.
Add the tofu and garam masala and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until hot and lightly dry.
Garnish with coriander. Toast the bread on a dry tawa or in a toaster and serve with the bhurji.

ing: 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/4 tsp red chilli powder, 1/4 tsp garam masala
1 tbsp mint chutney made with mint, coriander, green chilli and lemon juice
steps: Heat oil, add onion and chilli and saute until soft. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the chicken mince and break it up with a spoon. Cook on medium 5 minutes until it turns white all over.
Add tomato, spices and salt, cover and cook 6-8 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked with no pink left and the mix is dry.
Stir in coriander and let it cool slightly.
Spread mint chutney on the bread, add the keema, cucumber and tomato, and close the sandwich.
Toast on a dry tawa for 1-2 minutes per side, pressing gently, and cut in half.

ing: 1 ripe banana (frozen in slices for a thicker bowl)
A few banana slices and 1 tsp extra oats (topping)
steps: Dry roast the oats in a pan for 2 minutes until lightly golden; keep 1 tsp aside for topping.
Blend the banana, peanut butter, milk, curd, roasted oats and cinnamon until thick and smooth.
Pour into a bowl. Add a splash of milk only if the blender struggles.
Top with banana slices, chopped peanuts and the reserved oats, and eat immediately.
Wash the guava well and cut into wedges, removing the hard stem end.
Sprinkle black salt, chilli powder and lemon juice over the guava.
Place the roasted chana in a bowl next to the guava.
Eat together; chew the chana well.
Rinse the sprouts and steam or boil them for 3-4 minutes until just tender; drain and cool.
Add onion, tomato, cucumber, carrot, chilli and coriander.
Sprinkle roasted cumin powder and black salt.
Squeeze the lemon over, toss well and serve right away.

ing: 1 cup (150 g) mixed chopped fruit (apple, papaya, banana, pomegranate, orange)
steps: Wash the fruits and cut them into bite-sized pieces.
Put them in a bowl and sprinkle chaat masala and roasted cumin powder.
Add the lemon juice and mint leaves.
Toss gently and eat within 15 minutes so the fruit stays fresh.
Remove the seeds from the dates and chop them. If they are hard, soak in 2 tbsp warm milk for 10 minutes.
Peel and slice the banana.
Blend banana, dates, milk and cardamom until smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink fresh.
Heat ghee in a pan on low, add makhana and roast, stirring, for 6-8 minutes until they crunch when pressed.
Turn off the heat, sprinkle turmeric, pepper and salt and toss. Let them cool so they stay crisp.
Whisk curd with cold water until smooth.
Stir in cumin powder, black salt, salt, ginger and mint.
Serve the buttermilk with the roasted makhana.

ing: Chikki (makes about 6 pieces; 1 serving = 2 pieces, about 30 g): 1/2 cup (75 g) raw peanuts
steps: Dry roast the peanuts on low heat for 6-8 minutes, cool, rub off the skins and split them roughly.
Grease a plate and a rolling pin with oil.
Melt the jaggery with 1 tsp water on low heat, stirring, for 3-4 minutes until it thickens. Drop a little into cold water; if it turns hard and snaps, it is ready.
Turn off the heat and quickly mix in the peanuts. Melted jaggery is extremely hot: do not touch it or taste it.
Pour onto the greased plate, flatten with the rolling pin and cut into 6 pieces while warm.
Once cool and hard, eat 2 pieces with the orange. Store the rest in an airtight box.
Place the eggs in a pan and cover with water by 1 inch.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 10 minutes.
Lift the eggs out with a spoon into cold water (careful, hot water) and leave 3 minutes.
Peel, cut in halves and sprinkle with pepper, salt and chilli powder.
Cut the pomegranate and tap the back with a spoon over a bowl to release the arils; remove the white pith.
Whisk the curd lightly until smooth.
Top with the pomegranate arils.
Add a pinch of roasted cumin and salt if you like it savoury, and eat chilled.
Wash the papaya, peel it, scoop out the seeds and cut into cubes.
Squeeze lemon juice over the papaya if you like.
Pour the coconut water into a glass; if using a whole tender coconut, ask an adult to open it, as the knife is heavy and sharp.
Drink the coconut water fresh with the papaya on the side.

ing: 1 cup (240 ml) unsweetened soy milk (fortified with calcium if possible)
steps: Shake the soy milk carton well and pour 1 cup into a glass.
Warm it for 1 minute if you prefer it hot, or drink it chilled.
Peel the banana.
Have the banana with the soy milk.
Dry roast the almonds, walnuts and seeds in a pan on low heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. Do not let them burn.
Spread on a plate to cool completely.
Mix with the peanuts and raisins.
Eat this small handful; make a week's batch and store it in an airtight jar.
Wash the sweet potato and pressure cook with 1 cup water for 2-3 whistles (or boil 15 minutes) until a knife slides in easily. Let pressure drop before opening.
Cool slightly, peel and cut into cubes.
Add onion, tomato, green chilli and coriander.
Sprinkle cumin powder, black salt, chilli powder and salt.
Squeeze the lime over, toss gently and serve warm.

ing: 1/3 cup (60 g) dry rajma, soaked overnight (or 1 cup / 170 g canned rajma, rinsed)
1/3 cup (60 g) raw rice (3/4 cup cooked)
1 small onion, chopped (half for curry, half for salad)
1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 1/2 tsp coriander powder
steps: Drain soaked rajma and pressure cook with 1.5 cups water and a pinch of salt for 5-6 whistles until very soft; let pressure drop fully before opening (skip if using canned).
Wash rice and cook with 2/3 cup water until fluffy.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin, then half the onion and saute until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato, turmeric, chilli and coriander powder; cook until soft and mushy.
Add rajma with some cooking water, mash a few beans, simmer 10 min until thick; stir in garam masala and salt.
Mix remaining onion with lemon juice, salt and coriander for the salad; serve with rice and rajma.

ing: 1/3 cup (60 g) dry kabuli chana, soaked overnight (or 1 cup / 165 g canned chickpeas, rinsed)
2 tsp oil (1 for chole, 1 for rice)
1/2 cucumber, sliced; pinch of salt and lemon juice
steps: Pressure cook soaked chana with 1.5 cups water and a pinch of salt for 5-6 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening (skip if canned).
For jeera rice: heat 1 tsp oil, add 1/2 tsp cumin, add washed rice and 2/3 cup water with salt; cover and cook on low until done.
For chole: heat 1 tsp oil, add remaining cumin and onion, saute until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste, tomato, turmeric, chilli and chole masala; cook until soft.
Add chana with a little cooking water, mash a few, simmer 10 min until thick; add salt.
Sprinkle cucumber slices with salt and lemon; serve alongside chole and jeera rice.

ing: 1/2 cup mixed vegetables (drumstick, carrot, brinjal), chopped
1 small tomato, chopped; 2 tbsp chopped onion
1 tsp tamarind paste (or small lemon-sized tamarind soaked)
2 tsp oil (1 for sambar, 1 for poriyal)
1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp urad dal, few curry leaves, 1 dry red chilli
1 cup (100 g) beans, finely chopped; 1 tbsp grated coconut
steps: Pressure cook rice and toor dal together with 2 cups water and turmeric for 4 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening.
Boil vegetables, onion and tomato in 1/2 cup water with tamarind, sambar powder and salt for 8 min.
Mash the rice-dal, add it to the vegetables, and simmer 3-4 min to a soft porridge-like consistency.
Temper 1 tsp oil with half the mustard, curry leaves and red chilli (plus GF hing if using); pour over sambar rice.
For poriyal: heat 1 tsp oil, add remaining mustard and urad dal, add beans, salt and 2 tbsp water; cover and cook 6-8 min.
Stir coconut into the beans and serve with sambar rice and a bowl of curd.

ing: 1/4 cup (45 g) toor or moong dal, washed
1 cup (100 g) bhindi, washed, dried and sliced
1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 1/2 tsp coriander powder
2 tsp oil (1 for tadka, 1 for bhindi)
steps: Pressure cook dal with 1 cup water and turmeric for 3 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening, then whisk smooth with salt.
Knead atta with a pinch of salt and water into a soft dough; rest 10 min.
For bhindi: heat 1/2 tsp oil, add half the onion, then bhindi, chilli, coriander powder and salt; cook uncovered on medium 10-12 min until not sticky.
For tadka: heat 1/2 tsp oil, add cumin, hing, garlic, rest of onion and tomato; cook soft and pour into the dal. Simmer 2 min.
Roll dough into 2 thin rotis and cook on a hot tawa, flipping until puffed with brown spots; brush lightly with remaining oil if you like.
Garnish dal with coriander and serve with rotis and bhindi.

ing: 1/3 cup (60 g) rice (Kerala matta or any rice)
1 cup mixed vegetables for avial (carrot, beans, raw banana, yam), cut into fingers
1/2 cup (50 g) cabbage, finely shredded (for thoran)
3 tbsp grated coconut (2 for avial, 1 for thoran), 1 green chilli
1/4 cup sambar vegetables (drumstick, pumpkin), 1 small tomato
1/2 tsp mustard seeds, few curry leaves
steps: Cook rice in plenty of water until soft and drain (or pressure cook with 1 cup water, 3 whistles, letting pressure drop before opening).

Sambar: pressure cook dal with 3/4 cup water and turmeric for 3 whistles (let pressure drop). Boil sambar vegetables, tomato, tamarind, sambar powder and salt, add dal, simmer 5 min, temper with 1 tsp oil, some mustard and curry leaves.
Avial: cook avial vegetables with a pinch of turmeric, salt and 1/4 cup water until just tender.
Grind 2 tbsp coconut with green chilli coarsely; add to avial with curd, mix gently on low heat for 2 min, switch off and drizzle 1 tsp coconut oil and curry leaves.
Thoran: heat 1 tsp oil, splutter remaining mustard, add cabbage, salt and 1 tbsp coconut; stir-fry 5 min.
Serve rice with sambar, avial and thoran.

ing: 1/2 cup mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas, capsicum), chopped
1.5 tsp bisi bele bath powder (check label: gluten-free)
1/2 tsp mustard seeds, few curry leaves, 6 cashews or 1 tbsp peanuts
Raita: 1/2 cup (120 g) curd, 1/4 cucumber grated, pinch roasted cumin powder
steps: Pressure cook rice, dal, vegetables and turmeric with 2.25 cups water for 4 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening.
Mash lightly, add tomato, tamarind, bisi bele powder and salt; simmer 5 min, adding hot water if too thick.
Heat ghee, add mustard, curry leaves and cashews or peanuts (and GF hing if using); fry until nuts turn golden.
Pour tempering over the bisi bele bath and mix.
For raita, whisk curd with cucumber, salt and cumin powder; serve with the hot bath.

ing: 1/4 cup (45 g) foxtail or little millet, washed
Kadhi: 1/2 cup (120 g) curd, 1 tbsp (10 g) besan (gram flour), 3/4 cup water
2 tsp oil (1 for khichdi, 1 for kadhi)
1 tsp cumin seeds (split), 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, few curry leaves
1/2 tsp grated ginger, 1 green chilli slit
steps: Heat 1 tsp oil in a pressure cooker, add 1/2 tsp cumin and ginger, then millet, dal, vegetables, a pinch of turmeric, salt and 1.5 cups water.
Pressure cook 3 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening and stir to a soft khichdi.
Whisk curd, besan, a pinch of turmeric and water until no lumps remain.
Bring kadhi to a boil on medium, stirring constantly so it does not split, then simmer 8-10 min until slightly thick; add salt.
Heat 1 tsp oil, add mustard, remaining cumin, curry leaves, green chilli (and GF hing if using); pour over kadhi.
Serve khichdi with hot kadhi.

ing: 1/3 cup (60 g) basmati rice, soaked 15 min
1/2 cup mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas), chopped
1 bay leaf, 2 cloves, 1 small cinnamon piece
1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 1/2 tsp coriander powder
2 tsp oil (1 for pulao, 1 for curry)
steps: Boil soya chunks in water for 5 min, drain, cool and squeeze out water.
Pulao: heat 1 tsp oil, add bay leaf, cloves, cinnamon and half the onion; saute 2 min.
Add vegetables, drained rice, salt and 2/3 cup water; cover and cook on low 12-15 min until rice is done.
Curry: heat 1 tsp oil, add cumin and remaining onion, saute golden; add ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook soft.
Add turmeric, chilli, coriander powder, garam masala, soya chunks, salt and 1/2 cup water; simmer 8 min until thick.
Garnish with coriander and serve curry with pulao.

ing: 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, pinch of hing
Salad: 1/4 cucumber, 1/2 carrot, few onion slices, lemon juice
steps: Knead atta with a pinch of salt and water into a soft dough; rest 10 min.
Blanch spinach and green chilli in boiling water for 2 min, rinse in cold water and blend to a puree.
Heat oil, add cumin and hing, then onion; saute golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook soft.
Add turmeric, spinach puree, salt and 2 tbsp water; simmer 4 min, then add paneer and garam masala and cook 2 min more.
Roll 2 thin rotis and cook on a hot tawa until puffed with brown spots.
Slice cucumber, carrot and onion, toss with lemon and salt; serve with palak paneer and rotis.

ing: 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 1/4 tsp garam masala
1/4 capsicum and 1/4 onion, cut into strips
1/2 cup (60 g) whole-wheat atta (for 1 large or 2 small wraps)
2 tbsp shredded cabbage or lettuce, few onion rings
Salt to taste, squeeze of lemon
steps: Mix curd, ginger-garlic paste, spices, salt and lemon; coat paneer, capsicum and onion and rest 10 min.
Knead atta with salt and water into a soft dough; rest while paneer marinates.
Heat oil in a pan and cook the paneer and vegetables on medium-high 5-6 min, turning until charred at the edges.
Roll the dough into a large thin round and cook on a hot tawa on both sides until spotted.
Spread chutney on the wrap, add cabbage, onion rings and paneer tikka, then roll up tightly and cut in half.

ing: 3/4 cup (150 g) cooked rice (from 1/3 cup raw), cooled
1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp urad dal, 1/2 tsp chana dal
1 green chilli, few curry leaves, 1/2 tsp grated ginger
2 tsp oil (1 for rice, 1 for sundal)
1/3 cup (60 g) dry kabuli or kala chana, soaked overnight (or 1 cup / 165 g canned, rinsed)
1 tbsp grated coconut, 1 dry red chilli
steps: Pressure cook soaked chana with water and a pinch of salt for 5-6 whistles until tender; let pressure drop fully before opening and drain (skip if canned).
Lemon rice: heat 1 tsp oil, add peanuts and fry until golden, then half the mustard, urad dal, chana dal, green chilli, ginger and curry leaves (and GF hing if using).
Add turmeric, switch off, add rice, salt and lemon juice; mix gently.
Sundal: heat 1 tsp oil, splutter remaining mustard with red chilli and curry leaves, add chana and salt and toss 2 min.
Stir in coconut and coriander; serve with lemon rice.

ing: 1/3 cup (60 g) raw rice (cooked very soft)
2-3 tbsp milk (keeps it from turning sour)
1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp urad dal, few curry leaves
1/2 tsp grated ginger, 1 green chilli chopped (optional)
steps: Cook rice with 1 cup water until very soft (pressure cook 3 whistles if you like, letting pressure drop before opening); mash lightly and cool until just warm.
Mix rice with curd, milk and salt until creamy.
Heat oil, add mustard, urad dal, curry leaves, ginger and green chilli; fry until dal turns golden.
Pour tempering over the rice, add grated carrot and mix.
Top with pomegranate and coriander; serve cool.

ing: 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder
Salad: 1/4 cucumber, 1/2 carrot, few onion rings, lemon juice
steps: Wash rice and cook with 2/3 cup water until fluffy.
Boil eggs for 10 min, cool in cold water, peel and make 2 shallow slits on each.
Heat oil, add cumin and onion; saute golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook until mushy.
Add turmeric, chilli, coriander powder and salt; cook 1 min, add 1/2 cup water and simmer 5 min.
Add eggs and garam masala, simmer 3 min so the gravy coats them.
Slice salad vegetables, toss with lemon and salt; serve with egg curry and rice.

ing: 120 g boneless chicken (breast or thigh), cut into strips
1/2 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp cumin powder, lemon juice
3 tbsp (35 g) moong or toor dal
1 small tomato, chopped; 1 garlic clove chopped
steps: Mix curd, ginger-garlic paste, spices, lemon and salt; coat chicken and marinate 30 min (or overnight in the fridge).
Pressure cook dal with 1 cup water and a pinch of turmeric for 3 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening and whisk with salt.
Jeera rice: heat 1 tsp oil, add 1/2 tsp cumin, add washed rice, 2/3 cup water and salt; cover and cook on low until done.
Heat a grill pan or tawa with 1 tsp oil and cook chicken on medium-high 5-6 min per side until no pink remains inside.
Dal tadka: heat 1 tsp oil, add remaining cumin, garlic, tomato (and GF hing if using); cook soft and pour into dal, simmer 2 min.
Serve grilled chicken with jeera rice and dal.

ing: 1/2 tsp ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric
1/3 cup (60 g) basmati rice, soaked 20 min
1 bay leaf, 2 cloves, 1 cardamom, small cinnamon piece
1 tbsp each chopped mint and coriander
Raita: 1/2 cup (120 g) curd, 2 tbsp chopped onion and cucumber, pinch roasted cumin
steps: Marinate chicken with curd, ginger-garlic paste, chilli, turmeric, biryani masala and salt for 30 min.
Heat oil in a pressure cooker, add whole spices and onion; saute until deep golden.
Add tomato and cook soft, then add chicken and cook 6-8 min, stirring, until it changes colour.
Add drained rice, mint, coriander, salt and 2/3 cup water; stir once gently.
Pressure cook 2 whistles on medium; let pressure drop fully before opening and fluff with a fork. Check chicken is cooked through.
Whisk raita ingredients with salt and serve with biryani.

ing: 1/3 cup (60 g) dry kala chana, soaked overnight (or 1 cup / 165 g boiled kala chana)
1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 1 tsp coriander powder
Salad: 1/4 cucumber, 1 small tomato, few onion slices, lemon juice, coriander
steps: Pressure cook soaked kala chana with 1.5 cups water and a pinch of salt for 6-7 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening (skip if pre-boiled).
Wash rice and cook with 2/3 cup water until fluffy.
Heat oil, add cumin and onion, saute golden; add ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook mushy.
Add turmeric, chilli, coriander powder, chana with 1/2 cup cooking water and salt; simmer 10 min, mashing a few chana to thicken. Stir in garam masala.
Chop salad vegetables, toss with lemon, salt and coriander; serve with rice and curry.

ing: 1/3 cup (60 g) basmati rice, soaked 20 min
3/4 cup mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas, potato, cauliflower), chopped
1 bay leaf, 2 cloves, 1 cardamom, small cinnamon piece
1 tbsp each chopped mint and coriander
Kachumber: 1/4 cucumber, 1 small tomato, 2 tbsp onion, all finely diced; lemon juice
steps: Heat oil in a pressure cooker, add whole spices and onion; saute until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and tomato, cook soft; add vegetables, curd, chilli, turmeric, biryani masala and salt and cook 3 min.
Add drained rice, mint, coriander and 2/3 cup water; stir gently once.
Pressure cook 2 whistles on medium; let pressure drop fully before opening and fluff with a fork.
Mix kachumber vegetables with lemon juice and salt; serve with biryani.

ing: 1/4 cup (45 g) yellow moong dal, washed
1/2 cup (60 g) jowar flour (makes 2 rotis), plus warm water
1 small onion, chopped (split); 1 small tomato, chopped
1/4 tsp turmeric (split), 1/2 tsp chilli powder, 1/2 tsp coriander powder
2 tsp oil (1 for dal, 1 for aloo gobi)
steps: Pressure cook moong dal with 1 cup water and a pinch of turmeric for 2-3 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening and whisk with salt.
Aloo gobi: heat 1 tsp oil, add 1/2 tsp cumin and half the onion, then potato, cauliflower, turmeric, chilli, coriander powder and salt; cover and cook on low 12-15 min, stirring, until tender.
Dal tadka: heat 1 tsp oil, add remaining cumin, garlic, ginger, rest of onion and tomato; cook soft and pour into the dal, simmer 2 min.
Mix jowar flour with salt and add warm water little by little, kneading with your palm into a smooth dough.
Pat each ball into a thin round between two sheets of plastic or on a floured board, cook on a hot tawa, sprinkle water on top, flip and press with a cloth to puff.
Serve rotis with moong dal and aloo gobi, garnished with coriander.

ing: 120 g fish pieces (rohu, seer or basa), cleaned
1/4 tsp turmeric (split), 1/2 tsp chilli powder for rubbing
1 tsp coriander powder, 1/2 tsp chilli powder
1/2 tsp mustard seeds, few curry leaves
1 cup mixed vegetables (beans, carrot, cabbage), chopped
2 tsp oil (1 for curry, 1 for vegetables)
steps: Rub fish with a pinch of turmeric, chilli and salt; rest 10 min.
Wash rice and cook with 2/3 cup water until fluffy.
Heat 1 tsp oil, add half the mustard, curry leaves and onion; saute golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and tomato and cook mushy.
Add coriander powder, chilli, remaining turmeric, tamarind, salt and 3/4 cup water; boil 5 min.
Slide in fish, cover and simmer gently 6-8 min without stirring hard, until fish flakes easily.
Vegetables: heat 1 tsp oil, splutter remaining mustard, add vegetables, salt and 2 tbsp water; cover and cook 6-8 min. Serve with rice and fish curry.

ing: 3/4 cup (120 g) sweet corn kernels (frozen or fresh)
steps: Boil or steam the corn for 4-5 minutes until tender, then drain.
Let the corn cool for 2 minutes in a bowl.
Add onion, tomato and cucumber.
Sprinkle chilli powder, chaat masala and salt.
Squeeze lime juice on top, add coriander, mix and eat fresh.
Heat oil in a pan on low flame.
Add makhana and roast, stirring often, for 6-7 minutes until crisp (one should crunch when pressed).
Turn off the flame and add turmeric, chilli powder, chaat masala and salt.
Toss well to coat.
Cool for 2 minutes so they stay crunchy, then eat.
Boil peanuts in salted water for 10-12 minutes until soft (or pressure cook 2 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening).
Drain and cool the peanuts.
Mix in onion, tomato, chilli powder, chaat masala and salt.
Add lime juice and coriander and toss.
Peel the banana and eat it alongside the chaat.

ing: 1/2 cup (90 g) boiled black chana (kala chana, soaked overnight)
steps: If not already cooked, pressure cook soaked chana with salt for 4-5 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening, then drain.
Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds; step back as they splutter.
Add urad dal, red chilli, curry leaves and hing (if using); stir until dal turns golden.
Add the chana and salt and toss for 2 minutes.
Turn off the flame, mix in coconut and serve warm.

ing: 1/2 cup (50 g) moong sprouts, steamed 3 min
steps: Steam or briefly boil the sprouts for 3 minutes and cool.
In a large bowl, mix sprouts, onion, tomato and carrot.
Add chilli powder, chaat masala, salt and lime juice and mix.
Add puffed rice and coriander just before eating so it stays crisp.
Toss and eat immediately (skip sev and papdi, which contain flour).
Whisk ragi flour into the water in a small pan until no lumps remain.
Add milk and place on medium-low flame.
Stir continuously for 5-6 minutes until it thickens and smells cooked.
Turn off the flame and stir in jaggery (if using) and cardamom.
Let it cool slightly before drinking; it will be hot.

ing: Mint dip: 3 tbsp (45 g) curd, 8-10 mint leaves (finely chopped), pinch salt, pinch cumin powder
steps: Mix curd, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala, turmeric, oil and salt in a bowl.
Add paneer, capsicum and onion, coat well and rest 10 minutes.
Thread onto skewers or spread on a tray.
Air-fry at 200 C for 8-10 minutes, or cook on a hot tawa 2-3 minutes per side, until edges brown.
For the dip, stir chopped mint, salt and cumin into curd.
Serve tikka warm with the mint dip.

ing: 2 slices whole wheat bread (dairy-free, check label)
1 tsp green chutney or a few coriander leaves
steps: Boil the egg for 10 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and slice.
Brush the outside of the bread lightly with oil.
On the inside of one slice spread chutney, then layer cucumber, tomato, carrot and egg.
Sprinkle salt and pepper and close with the second slice.
Toast on a tawa 2 minutes per side, pressing gently, until golden.
Cut in half and eat warm.

ing: 1 tsp olive oil or any oil
steps: Put chickpeas, tahini, lime juice, garlic, cumin and salt in a mixer jar.
Blend, adding water a spoon at a time, until smooth and creamy.
Spoon into a bowl and drizzle the oil on top.
Wash and cut the carrot and cucumber into finger-length sticks.
Dip the sticks into the hummus and eat.

ing: Pinch dried herbs or cumin powder
steps: Cut the sweet potato (skin on) into thin wedges.
Toss with oil, chilli powder, pepper, herbs and salt.
Spread in one layer in an air-fryer basket or on an oven tray.
Air-fry at 200 C for 15-18 minutes (or bake 25 minutes), turning halfway, until soft inside and browned.
Squeeze lime on top and let cool 2 minutes before eating.

ing: 2 slices whole wheat bread (dairy-free and egg-free, check label)
steps: Toast the bread on a tawa or toaster until crisp.
Spread peanut butter evenly on both slices.
Arrange banana slices on top.
Sprinkle cinnamon if using and eat right away.

ing: 100 g boneless chicken, cut into bite-size cubes
1/4 onion and 1/4 capsicum, cut in squares
steps: Mix curd, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, garam masala, turmeric, lime juice, oil and salt.
Add chicken, coat well and marinate at least 20 minutes in the fridge.
Thread chicken, onion and capsicum onto skewers (soak wooden skewers in water 10 minutes first).
Air-fry at 200 C for 12-15 minutes, or cook on a hot tawa turning often, until browned.
Cut the thickest piece open: cook until no pink remains and juices run clear.
Wash hands and boards after handling raw chicken; serve hot.

ing: Roti: 1/2 cup (60 g) whole wheat atta, about 1/4 cup (60 ml) water, pinch salt
Dal: 1/4 cup (50 g) toor or moong dal, washed
Sabzi: 1 cup (120 g) mixed chopped vegetables (carrot, beans, peas, cabbage)
steps: Pressure cook dal with water and turmeric for 3 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening.
Heat 1 tsp oil, add cumin and hing, then tomato; cook 2 minutes, pour in the dal, add salt and simmer 3 minutes.
For sabzi, heat 1 tsp oil, add mustard or cumin seeds, then vegetables, chilli powder and salt; cover and cook 8-10 minutes until tender.
Knead atta, salt and water into a soft dough and rest 5 minutes.
Divide into 2 balls, roll thin and cook each on a hot tawa about 1 minute per side until brown spots appear.
Serve rotis with dal and sabzi.

ing: 1/2 cup (60 g) chopped vegetables (carrot, peas, beans)
steps: Wash rice and dal together twice and drain.
Heat oil in a small pressure cooker, add cumin, hing (if using) and ginger.
Add vegetables, turmeric and salt and stir 1 minute.
Add rice, dal and water; close and cook 3 whistles.
Let pressure drop fully before opening; stir and add a little hot water if too thick.
Serve warm with curd on the side.

ing: Jowar roti: 1/2 cup (60 g) jowar flour, about 1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, pinch salt
Palak dal: 1/4 cup (50 g) toor or moong dal, washed
steps: Pressure cook dal with water and turmeric for 3 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening.
Heat oil, add cumin and garlic, then palak; cook 2 minutes until wilted.
Add the dal, chilli powder and salt and simmer 3-4 minutes.
Mix jowar flour and salt with hot water (careful, it is hot) using a spoon, then knead into a smooth dough when cool enough to touch.
Pat or roll 2 small rotis between two sheets of plastic or on a dusted board.
Cook on a hot tawa, sprinkling a little water on top, about 1-2 minutes per side until cooked; serve with palak dal.

ing: Mudde: 1/3 cup (40 g) ragi flour, 1/2 cup (120 ml) water, pinch salt
Sambar: 1/4 cup (50 g) toor dal, washed
1/2 cup (60 g) chopped vegetables (drumstick, carrot, brinjal, onion)
1 tsp tamarind paste (or small lemon-size tamarind soaked)
steps: Pressure cook dal with water and turmeric for 3 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening and mash.
Boil vegetables in 1/2 cup water with tamarind, sambar powder and salt for 6-8 minutes; add the dal and simmer 3 minutes.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and curry leaves, let splutter (step back) and pour into the sambar.
For mudde, boil the 1/2 cup water with salt, add ragi flour all at once and do not stir for 1 minute.
Stir hard with a wooden spoon on low flame 3-4 minutes until a smooth thick ball forms.
Wet your hands with cold water, shape into a ball once warm (not hot), and serve with sambar.

ing: 1/2 cup (60 g) chopped vegetables (carrot, peas, beans, tomato)
steps: Wash dalia and dal and drain.
Heat oil in a small pressure cooker; add cumin, hing and ginger.
Add dalia and roast 1 minute, then add vegetables, turmeric and salt.
Add dal and water, close and cook 3 whistles.
Let pressure drop fully before opening; stir and add hot water if too thick.
Serve warm.

ing: 1 cup (150 g) lauki (bottle gourd), peeled and diced
steps: Cook rice with water in a covered pot 12-15 minutes (or 2 whistles in a cooker) until soft.
Boil masoor dal with water and turmeric 12-15 minutes until soft (or 2 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening).
Heat 1 tsp oil, add cumin, garlic and tomato, cook 2 minutes, add dal and salt and simmer 3 minutes.
For sabzi, heat 1 tsp oil, add mustard seeds, then lauki, chilli powder and salt.
Cover and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring once, until lauki is soft.
Serve rice with dal and lauki sabzi.

ing: 1 cup (120 g) sliced vegetables (capsicum, onion, carrot, beans)
Roti: 1/2 cup (60 g) whole wheat atta, about 1/4 cup (60 ml) water, pinch salt
steps: Knead atta, salt and water into a soft dough and rest 5 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan on high, add ginger-garlic paste and stir 30 seconds.
Add vegetables and stir-fry 4-5 minutes so they stay slightly crunchy.
Add paneer, tomato puree, chilli powder, pepper and salt; toss gently 2 minutes.
Roll the dough into 2 thin rotis and cook on a hot tawa about 1 minute per side until brown spots appear.
Serve the stir-fry with rotis.

ing: 2 cups (480 ml) water for boiling chunks
1/3 cup (60 g) rice, washed, with 2/3 cup (160 ml) water
steps: Cook rice with water in a covered pot 12-15 minutes until soft.
Boil soya chunks in water for 5 minutes, drain, cool slightly and squeeze out the water.
Heat oil, add cumin, then onion; cook until golden, then add ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt; cook until soft and mushy.
Add soya chunks, garam masala and water; simmer covered 5-6 minutes.
Top with coriander and serve with rice.

ing: 1 cup (150 g) cooked rice, preferably cooled
3/4 cup (90 g) chopped vegetables (carrot, beans, capsicum, cabbage, spring onion)
steps: Pat tofu dry with a cloth.
Heat 1/2 tsp oil in a pan and cook tofu 3-4 minutes, turning, until lightly golden; remove.
Add remaining oil and garlic, then vegetables; stir-fry on high 3-4 minutes.
Add rice, soy sauce, pepper and a little salt (soy sauce is already salty).
Return tofu, toss 2 minutes until hot and serve.

ing: Roti: 1/2 cup (60 g) whole wheat atta, about 1/4 cup (60 ml) water, pinch salt
Salad: 1/2 cucumber, 1/2 tomato, 1/4 onion sliced, lime and salt
steps: Knead atta, salt and water into a soft dough and rest 5 minutes.
Heat oil, cook onion and green chilli until soft, then add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt.
Beat the eggs, pour into the pan and stir gently 2-3 minutes until fully set with no runny egg.
Mix in coriander and turn off the flame.
Roll 2 thin rotis and cook on a hot tawa about 1 minute per side.
Slice the salad vegetables, add lime and salt, and serve with bhurji and roti.

ing: 120 g chicken pieces (boneless or small bone-in)
Roti: 1/2 cup (60 g) whole wheat atta, about 1/4 cup (60 ml) water, pinch salt
Salad: 1/2 cucumber, 1/2 carrot, lime and salt
steps: Heat oil, add cumin and onion and cook until golden; add ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt; cook until soft.
Add chicken and stir 3 minutes, then add water, cover and simmer 15-20 minutes.
Cut the thickest piece open: cook until no pink remains; stir in garam masala.
Meanwhile knead atta, salt and water into dough, roll 2 rotis and cook on a hot tawa about 1 minute per side.
Slice cucumber and carrot, add lime and salt, and serve with curry and roti.

ing: 1 fish fillet or steak (100-120 g), e.g. seer, pomfret or basa
1/3 cup (60 g) rice, washed, with 2/3 cup (160 ml) water
Beans: 1 cup (100 g) chopped beans, 1 tsp oil, 1/4 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp urad dal, 1 tbsp grated coconut
steps: Cook rice with water in a covered pot 12-15 minutes until soft.
Rub fish with turmeric, chilli powder, lime juice, ginger-garlic paste and salt; rest 10 minutes, then dust with rice flour.
For beans, heat 1 tsp oil, add mustard seeds and urad dal, then beans, salt and a splash of water; cover and cook 6-8 minutes, then add coconut.
Heat 1 tsp oil on a tawa on medium; place fish gently away from you to avoid splashes.
Cook 3-4 minutes per side until golden and the fish flakes easily with a fork.
Serve fish with rice and beans.

ing: Appam: 1/2 cup (70 g) rice flour, 1/4 cup (60 ml) thin coconut milk, 1/4 cup (60 ml) warm water, 1/4 tsp instant yeast, pinch sugar, pinch salt
2 cloves, 1 small cinnamon stick, 2 cardamom pods
steps: For appam, mix rice flour, yeast, sugar, salt, coconut milk and warm water into a smooth pouring batter; cover and rest 1 hour until bubbly.
For stew, heat oil, add whole spices, curry leaves, onion, ginger and green chilli; cook 2 minutes without browning.
Add chicken, potato, carrot, salt and thin coconut milk; cover and simmer 15-20 minutes until vegetables are soft and no pink remains in the chicken.
Lower the flame, stir in thick coconut milk and pepper and heat 1 minute without boiling.
Heat a small non-stick pan or appachatti, pour a ladle of batter and swirl to coat the sides; cover and cook 2 minutes until the edges are crisp and the centre is set.
Make 2-3 appams and serve hot with the stew.

ing: 1/3 cup (60 g) dry rajma, soaked overnight (or 3/4 cup boiled rajma)
Roti: 1/2 cup (60 g) whole wheat atta, about 1/4 cup (60 ml) water, pinch salt
Kachumber: 1/2 cucumber, 1/2 tomato, 1/4 onion (all diced), lime, salt, coriander
steps: Pressure cook soaked rajma with water and salt for 6-7 whistles until very soft; let pressure drop fully before opening.
Heat oil, add cumin and hing, then onion until golden, then ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt; cook until mushy.
Add rajma with its water, mash a few beans, and simmer 8-10 minutes; finish with garam masala.
Knead atta, salt and water into dough, roll 2 rotis and cook on a hot tawa about 1 minute per side.
Mix the diced kachumber vegetables with lime, salt and coriander and serve with rajma and roti.

ing: Dosa: 3/4 cup (180 ml) fermented rice-urad dosa batter, 1 tsp oil
Sambar: 1/4 cup (50 g) toor dal, washed, with 1 cup (240 ml) water
1/2 cup (60 g) chopped vegetables (onion, drumstick, carrot, brinjal)
1 tsp oil, 1/4 tsp mustard seeds, 5-6 curry leaves (tempering)
Tomato chutney: 1 medium tomato chopped, 2 tbsp chopped onion, 1 dry red chilli, 1 tsp oil, 1/4 tsp mustard seeds, few curry leaves
steps: Pressure cook dal with water and turmeric for 3 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening, then mash.
Boil vegetables in 1/2 cup water with tamarind, sambar powder and salt for 6-8 minutes; add dal and simmer 3 minutes; temper with oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves (step back as they splutter).
For chutney, heat 1/2 tsp oil, cook onion, red chilli and tomato until soft; cool, grind with salt, then temper with remaining oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Heat a tawa on medium, pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread in circles.
Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edge and cook until the bottom is golden and crisp; fold.
Make 2-3 dosas and serve hot with sambar and tomato chutney.

ing: 1/3 cup (60 g) dry kabuli chana, soaked overnight (or 3/4 cup boiled chana)
1 1/2 cups (360 ml) water for cooking chana
1/3 cup (60 g) red rice, washed, with 1 cup (240 ml) water
steps: Pressure cook soaked chana with water and salt for 5-6 whistles until soft; let pressure drop fully before opening.
Pressure cook red rice with water for 4-5 whistles (or simmer covered 30-35 minutes) until tender.
Heat oil, add cumin, then onion until golden, then ginger-garlic paste.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt; cook until mushy.
Add chana with some cooking water, mash a few, and simmer 8-10 minutes; finish with garam masala and coriander.
Serve chana masala with red rice.

ing: 1/4 cup (50 g) mixed dal (toor, moong, masoor), washed
1/3 cup (60 g) rice, washed, with 2/3 cup (160 ml) water
1 tsp oil (for dal), 1/4 tsp cumin seeds, 1 garlic clove chopped, 2 tbsp chopped tomato
Cabbage poriyal: 1 cup (90 g) finely shredded cabbage
1 tsp oil, 1/4 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp urad dal, 5-6 curry leaves
steps: Pressure cook mixed dal with water and turmeric for 3-4 whistles; let pressure drop fully before opening.
Cook rice with water in a covered pot 12-15 minutes until soft.
Heat 1 tsp oil, add cumin, garlic and tomato; cook 2 minutes, add dal and salt and simmer 3 minutes.
For poriyal, heat 1 tsp oil, add mustard seeds (step back), urad dal, curry leaves and chilli.
Add cabbage and salt, cover and cook 5-6 minutes until just soft; mix in coconut.
Serve rice with dal and cabbage poriyal.
